//: Hand-written explanations, one sentence per system, merged into docs/library-status.md as the 'why' column. This file is written by people and read by render.lisp; the check run (run-quickload.sh) never touches it, which is the whole point -- a re-measurement rewrites 'note' from the raw error and would otherwise erase the reason behind it.
//published: Every sentence here is published verbatim in the table, so write it for a reader outside this repository: English, no internal issue numbers, and an issue reference only if it is an issue in the public dotcl/dotcl repository. Identifiers and error text are Markdown here, so wrap them in backticks: only the cell separator is escaped for you.
//scope: Say WHY the row looks the way it does, not what the error was -- 'note' already carries that. A row that needs no explanation has no entry here.
postmodern: `cl-postgres.asd` pulls usocket in through an allowlist of implementations but its code reaches for usocket through a denylist, so every implementation missing from that allowlist hits this; quickloading usocket first makes postmodern load unchanged.
chanl: The one failing check is `STUMBLERS` in `DEADLOCK`, and SBCL fails it the same way: it asks `yes-or-no-p`, and a test run with no terminal gets `END-OF-FILE` there instead of an answer.
sdl2: Not a dotcl failure: this host has no SDL2 library, so the loader finds neither the framework nor libSDL2. SBCL 2.6.8 stops at the same place.
hunchentoot: The failing checks are uploaded files coming back larger than they were sent: rfc2388, which parses the upload, writes the file as `latin-1` only on the implementations it lists and in the default external format (UTF-8) elsewhere, so every byte above 127 is written as two. With a fork of rfc2388 that adds dotcl to that list, the suite passes.
spatial-trees: The result varies from run to run: the suites build their trees from `random` rectangles and points, and of four runs with the same dotcl and dists, one failed 3 of 18 checks and three passed all of theirs (the run shown is one of these).
april: The Quicklisp dist's april release ships cape/cape.asd in its tarball but does not index it, so `(ql:quickload "april")` fails with `System "cape" not found` on SBCL as well. Loaded from the unpacked release tree instead, `(april (test))` passes 1140 of 1140 here.
hu.dwim.util: Loads; `source/place.lisp` warns at read time (`#.(warn ...)`) that `symbol-global-value` has no implementation outside SBCL and falls back to `symbol-value`.
hu.dwim.walker: Loads. Its test system needs iolib, which has no branch for dotcl's Gray streams, and, as on SBCL, the C library libfixposix, which the measuring machine does not have.
clx: Loads. Its tests connect to an X server, and the measuring machine has none (`DISPLAY` is not set); SBCL fails the same four. `dependent.lisp` still warns at compile time that `buffer-input-wait-default` falls back to polling on an implementation it has no code for.
magicl: Loads, but `with-array-pointers` signals an error while expanding on an implementation it does not know, so the tests stop at the first BLAS call. With a dotcl branch there the tests get as far as on SBCL, which stops in the LAPACK examples on `zuncsd_`, a routine the measuring machine's LAPACK does not export.
coalton: The released Coalton (2026-01-01) implements its hashing only for SBCL, Allegro and CCL and stops with `#.(error ...)` elsewhere, so it does not load. Coalton's upstream main supports dotcl, and the with forks column is measured from it: it loads in 51 seconds and its suite passes (698 checks), but building the test system takes 201 seconds and running the suite 481 (SBCL 2.6.8 on the same machine: 20, 70 and 53 seconds, with 757 checks including the thread tests dotcl does not run).
